description: Indian TDS rates, thresholds and due dates. Every rule carries the authority it comes from and the dates it applies between, so questions about past years are answerable and stale rules are visible.
maintenance: Review each February after the Union Budget, and whenever a Finance Act amends a section. Add a NEW rule with a later applies_from; never edit a past rule in place — that would silently rewrite history.
verified_against: GUIDE.md rate card FY2026-27, cross-checked against incometaxindia.gov.in and the new-Act payment code tables

rules.label: Salary
rules.notes: Computed on the employee's estimated annual income at slab rates, spread across the year. Not a flat rate — the calculator handles this, not this table.

rules.label: Professional fees
rules.description: Consultants, CA, lawyer, designer, recruiter, doctor, freelance developer
rules.notes: Once the year's aggregate crosses the threshold, TDS applies to the WHOLE aggregate including earlier untaxed invoices — not just the excess. Catch-up is required on those earlier payments.

rules.label: Technical services
rules.notes: Routine outsourced technical work, call centre. Distinguish from professional fees (10%) — the classification decides the rate.

rules.label: Director fees (sitting fees, non-salary)
rules.notes: NO threshold — applies from the first rupee. Also note: director services attract GST under reverse charge (Notification 13/2017), and s.24(iii) CGST compels registration for anyone liable under RCM regardless of turnover.
rules.authority: Income-tax Act 2025 s.393(1) (old s.194J); GST Notification 13/2017-CT(R)

rules.label: Contractor / job work — individual or HUF vendor
rules.notes: DUAL TEST: TDS applies if a SINGLE payment exceeds 30,000 OR the year's aggregate exceeds 1,00,000. Either trigger is sufficient.

rules.label: Contractor / job work — company, firm or LLP vendor
rules.notes: Same dual test as the individual case; only the rate differs by vendor entity type.

rules.label: Rent — land, building or furniture
rules.notes: THRESHOLD IS PER MONTH, NOT PER YEAR. Rent of 30,000/month is 3,60,000/year but stays BELOW the threshold and needs no TDS. Misreading this caused a real over-deduction in May 2026.

rules.label: Rent — plant, machinery or equipment
rules.notes: Distinct from land/building rent, which is 10% under code 1009. Choosing the wrong code applies the wrong rate.

rules.label: Interest paid (not bank interest)
rules.notes: Applies to interest on loans from persons or NBFCs. Bank interest paid by the company is outside this.

rules.label: Purchase of goods
rules.notes: Only applies if OUR turnover exceeded 10 crore in the previous FY. TDS is on the excess over 50 lakh, not the whole amount — unlike most other sections.

rules.label: Payment to partners (firm or LLP)
rules.notes: Salary, bonus, commission or interest paid by a firm/LLP to its partners. Not applicable to a private limited company.

rules.label: Any payment to a non-resident or foreign company
rules.notes: STOP. Rate depends on the payment's nature and the applicable DTAA. Forms 15CA/15CB are required. Never compute this automatically — hold the payment and consult a CA.

due_dates.label: Monthly TDS deposit
due_dates.exception: TDS deducted in March is due by 30 April, not 7 April

due_dates.label: Form 16A to deductee
due_dates.rule: 15 days after the return due date

interest_and_penalties.label: Interest — failure to deduct
interest_and_penalties.basis: part month counts as a full month

interest_and_penalties.label: Interest — deducted but deposited late
interest_and_penalties.basis: part month counts as a full month

interest_and_penalties.label: Late filing fee
interest_and_penalties.cap: cannot exceed the TDS amount in that statement

interest_and_penalties.label: Expense disallowance for non-deduction
interest_and_penalties.notes: 30% of the expense is disallowed for income tax. NOTE: this is a consequence of not deducting, NOT an alternative to deducting. The deductor remains liable under s.201 regardless, and a payee's losses or the payer's losses do not remove that liability.
